Robustness check with stronger GRUs (seed 0): the held-out verdict holds (GRU 128/8000: 1.9264, GRU 256/16000: 1.3825, learned prior 0.8907; counts 2.6306 vs 2.6132, inside the noise), but the in-distribution lead of the learned prior does not (GRU 256/16000: 0.1825 vs 0.2206). The noise-mode ablation of seed 0 also reproduces exactly (fixed noise 1.9935 on held-out families).

PI-01.notes: Mechanism verified: every predictive family's log-likelihood equals scipy (normal, student-t, Poisson with exposure, negative binomial, Bernoulli, categorical, discrete hazard vs geometric), predictions are action-conditioned and registered at two horizons on the real Qwen3-4B configuration, and they change when only experiential weights change (max relative change of the predicted means 0.15 % / 7.6 % for perturbations of 5 % / 50 % of each tensor's std; adapters, heads and reward bit-identical). Learning evidence is debug-scale only (B's 86 measured numbers bit-reproduce on the committed code); on new mechanisms the heads do not beat the action-independent baseline; nothing is trained on the real configuration; not called by the runtime.
evidence: B suite on the HEAD snapshot with CAM_LIVE_B_MEASURE: 142 passed, 86/86 measured values equal docs/evidence/B/measured.json

PI-08.notes: For policy, greedy, UCB, VOI-weighted and Thompson (posterior samples and normal marginals) the recorded Decision.probabilities are what the index is drawn from (chi-square p 0.055-0.93 over 20000 draws each), the infeasible candidate gets exactly 0, the eps floor holds; the mean Thompson propensity from normal marginals matches the true P(best) within 0.01; randomised assignment matches the recorded 0.3/0.7 within 4 se and is registered before the first assignment. Gaps (B's own): rules not compared on a task beyond greedy vs VOI. On the real configuration an experiential-only change moves the decision distribution (Thompson TV 0.061 at a 5 % perturbation; greedy/UCB argmax flips, TV 0.98, at 50 %; policy-rule TV only 8e-5 / 8.5e-4 because the policy head is near-uniform at initialisation).

PI-09.notes: On real Qwen3-4B the proposer produced 4 schema-valid backbone actions merged with 13 schema-walker candidates, every candidate carries its provenance and decisions record exact probabilities. But the backbone is NOT conditioned on the latent in effect: log p(completion | prompt, b) is bit-identical for two different beliefs at initialisation (bridge output projection zero); the path exists (|dlogp| = 0.87 after perturbing the bridge) and only D's consequence provider (credit/providers.py:632) can train it. Proposal usefulness not measured.

Residual risk B states itself: code outside B could wrap an imagined value in an ordinary observation. C's ledger screen does not read an OutcomeObservation.imagined field (the field is being added to the contract in the working tree).

RC-01.notes: Declared queries link exactly to their decision and queue it; equal window evidence splits 0.5/0.5 with uncertainty 0.5 kept into the simple credit; recency is not evidence (no evidence -> no link); a decision after the outcome is refused and its share stays unattributed; duplicate events are dropped; a verified copy replaces the unverified one; an outcome dated before its query is refused. REFUTED: an attribution map with a negative amount (by_action {a: 3, b: -1}, event value 2) gives a link weight 1.5 > 1 and credits 3.0 for an outcome of 2.0; b's -1 is silently dropped (defect M3, links.py:213-221).

RC-02.notes: ReturnDecomposer verified with random non-zero weights, padding, irregular times and beta in {0, 1e-4, 2e-3, 0.05}: signal = (G - F(H_<t))/Gamma_t, return-to-go identity, unmatured rows NaN and loss None, no gradient from unmatured rows, perturbing decisions >= j (latents and times) leaves pred[:, :j+1], signal[:, :j] and earlier contributions bit-identical. Gaps: (1) the redistributed credit is not consumed by any training update (spec 9.2 'use redistributed credit during eligible training updates'; D discloses); (2) trajectories longer than max_len (64): earlier decisions get no RUDDER credit and the window is discounted from its own first decision while G is referenced at the trajectory start (rudder_rtg 0.1273 vs 0.1579 expected after 10800 s at beta 2e-5; defect m3); (3) the validation of RUDDER against experiments is in-sample (M1, see RC-08).

RC-03.notes: sum_t Gamma_t c_t = G with Gamma_t = exp(-beta * (t_t - t_first)) recomputed independently: max error 0.0 (float64) for beta 0 .. 0.05 over 7 trajectories of length 1..13 with padding; D's Gamma equals the own one to 1e-12; trajectory_return G = sum of distinct events discounted to the first decision (own value equal to 1e-12, one event per dedup key). Caveat: for trajectories truncated to max_len the convention is applied to the window (m3).

RC-04.notes: Independent ground truth (own trajectory enumeration, own exact gradient by autograd, own hindsight coefficients w = p(a|s,u)/pi(a|s) - 1 with multiplicity counting, own Eq. 4 estimator) on key_to_door d3, noisy_key_to_door, two random trees: D's coefficients equal to 1e-15, D's cocoa_grad equal per trajectory to 4e-16, exact relative bias <= 1.2e-30. Monte Carlo with an own sampler, 200 seeds x 400 trajectories, z against the exact per-component variance: mean z^2 0.989 / 0.972 / 0.999 / 1.013 (SE 0.02-0.03), pooled max |z| inside the Bonferroni band; noisy rewards (key_to_door d4, sigma 0.5): pooled max |z| 2.43; a +0.3 bias in w is detected at |z| = 201 (the test can fail). Variance: COCOA below REINFORCE everywhere (exact trace 0.74 vs 4.65 etc.). Reproduced D's numbers: exact_rel_var_reinforce 23.458 (D 23.46), exact_rel_var_cocoa 10.517 (D 10.52), key-decision variance 8.03 / 0.0609 (D 8.09 / 0.0593, MC).

RC-05.notes: check_support refuses missing / NaN / >1 / unnormalised / near-zero / -inf propensities and open_ended-without-tracking, and the refused rows are NaN (not numbers); an untrained hindsight model claims w = 0; learned association / counterfactual estimate / experimental effect are separate fields (attach_experiment refuses non-randomised effects). Gaps: (m1) open-endedness is read only from decision.diagnostics['open_ended'] (default False) which no producer in the tree sets; ActionSpec.provenance ('backbone') is ignored, so backbone-generated candidate sets are 'supported' (probe D); (m2) the CAM extension's training pairs and credit sum exclude outcomes declared by an earlier decision but observed after t, which Eq. 4 includes (9 of 12 such pairs left out in one 6-decision lifetime): the extension is not the reference estimator's sum.

RC-06.notes: A matured declared outcome links to its decision and queues it for re-training; CreditAssigner withholds RUDDER/COCOA until the objective is closed and nothing goal-relevant is pending (open objective and pending query both keep the return unmatured), then writes versioned credit for all earlier decisions (6-decision door lifetime: credit present after closing). D's provider tests (default + slow) pass. Depends on the agent calling put_objective_outcome (D-10, not integrated).

RC-07.notes: Decision after the outcome refused as a cause; outcome before its query refused; audit_leakage reports exactly a planted future-dated context item and nothing else; put_item never replaces a stored item; RUDDER prefix predictions are bit-identical under perturbation of later decisions and times. Caveat (M2): SqliteExperienceStore.update() accepts a rewritten decision / context_item_refs / ts for a stored record; audit_leakage catches it only when the injected items are dated after the decision.

RC-08.notes: Mechanism exists (selector starts at 'simple', scores only randomised evidence, gate on mean z^2 / sign agreement), RUDDER and COCOA are exercised. REFUTED as 'selected by evidence': the experiments used to validate the estimators are the lifetimes they were trained on (71 % of the experiment records are in the learner's training split, compare_with_experiment uses all of them; D's synthetic selection test also trains and validates on the same data). In D's recorded LabWorld run the RUDDER estimate has standard error 0.0 in all 6 experiments: each arm's estimate is a single fitted value F(first decision | arm) regressed on the same returns that define the measured difference, so agreement is largely by construction (defect M1). The promotion of 'rudder' is not independent evidence; D itself reports it as unstable across seeds.

SE-02.notes: prefix_targets applies one signed outcome to every earlier prefix (prefixes at/after evaluation masked, 1/n weight per trajectory); unsigned refused; pending -> zero loss and gradient; an 80 % forecast that fails receives gradient p - y. SE-03.notes: Count magnitudes by negative binomial (== scipy, -> Poisson), time to achievement by a censoring-aware discrete hazard (== geometric; censored = survival of completed bins), resources by a normal on log1p. Accuracy only at debug scale.

SE-04.notes: Brier, NLL, reliability and slope/intercept are computed correctly on synthetic data with known calibration (true 0.7/0.3 inside the intervals) and predictions are prospective. DEFECT D5: the slope/intercept intervals ignore clustering (Brier/NLL use clusters): on a clustered null (40 lifetimes x 16 forecasts, true slope 0) the 95 % interval excludes 0 in 61 % of runs, so B's reported 'slope 254.16 (CI 122.43..385.90)' is not a valid interval. The trained evaluator does not beat the base rate (B).

SE-05.notes: action_quality = q[chosen] - E_pi q, regret, and quality + luck = surprise hold exactly; a lucky success of a poor decision has quality < 0, luck > 0. B reports that the raw outcome is the better indicator of true advantage at debug scale.

SE-06.notes: Reference VOI estimators are correct (E[max affine] and the knowledge gradient vs Monte Carlo; a decision-irrelevant observation with large surprise has VOI exactly 0) and the Predictor uses the Jensen gap E[max] - max E.
